subject: Onboarding: Acceptance sprint matrix, load rehearsal plan & evidence
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@paylane.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@paylane.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: Acceptance sprint matrix, load rehearsal plan & evidence

Hi Asha / Ravi —

Following our handoff call last week, attaching the acceptance sprint matrix and an initial load-rehearsal plan for PayLane's onboarding. Goal here is to make the acceptance window prescriptive so your SREs and ours can run a deterministic rehearsal and share machine-readable evidence.

High-level ask: please confirm two things by EOD Tuesday so we can lock the run window (Thu-Fri):
- Your preferred ramp profile (steady ramp vs. step-ramp) and peak concurrency target (e.g., 3k QPS, 10s median).
- Any environment constraints (IPs, allowed test CIDRs, or sampling constraints for PHI).

Attached: acceptance-sprint-matrix.xlsx (matrix with criteria + owner + evidence type), paylane-ramp-profiles.yml (example step/gradual profiles). We'll produce a CSV of raw results and a short readout after the run.

Next steps from our side once you confirm the ramp:
1) Marcus will schedule the run and provision an evaluation slot in our Dedicated pool.
2) Monica will share an evaluation checklist for telemetry and tracing (what to capture, span names).
3) I'll coordinate a 30-minute readout and a short acceptance decision email.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Asha Verma <asha@paylane.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@paylane.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Acceptance sprint matrix, load rehearsal plan & evidence

Thanks Lauren — this looks good. A few quick notes:
- We prefer a step-ramp profile that holds for 15 minutes at each step; peak concurrency target: 2,500 concurrent requests (we'll provide correct sampling keys for prod-like payloads).
- No PHI in the test payloads; we'll use anonymized records.
- Allowed test CIDR: 35.201.0.0/16 and 34.72.0.0/16 (our infra team whitelisted these).

Can Marcus propose two 2-hour windows on Thursday (UTC-friendly)? We have a release on Friday morning so anything late Friday is risky.

— Asha
Asha Verma
Head of Platform, PayLane
asha@paylane.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Acceptance sprint matrix, load rehearsal plan & evidence

Thanks Asha — noted on step-ramp and 2.5k target. Proposing two windows:
- Thu 2026-08-26 14:00–16:00 UTC (preferred)
- Thu 2026-08-26 20:00–22:00 UTC (backup; lower region overlap)

I'll reserve the Dedicated slot and pre-warm the KV caches ahead of the run to match your expected payload distribution. Monica / Ben: can you confirm the trace/span names we rely on and whether we should enable debug-level sampling for the first 10 minutes?

Attachment: paylane-ramp-profiles.yml (updated with Asha's peak).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Onboarding: Acceptance sprint matrix, load rehearsal plan & evidence

Marcus — quick confirmation:
- Trace/span names: "request.receive", "runtime.infer.token", "cache.kv.hit"; we'll include a short mapping table in the readout.
- Enable debug sampling for the first 10 minutes at 5% to gather tail-latency cases.
- We'll also enable token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency histograms; please confirm retention for these artifacts (we'll store for 30 days by default).

Asha — is 30-day retention OK for the telemetry artifacts? If not, we can redact or shorten retention.

— Monica

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@paylane.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@paylane.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance run results & next steps — PayLane (raw evidence attached)

Hi all —

Thanks for the run today. Quick summary and attached artifacts: latency-throughput-results-20260824.csv (raw samples), and a short artifact pack with dashboards and span mappings in the Drive link. Key observations:

- Peak sustained concurrency reached: 2,470 QPS (within 1.2% of target).
- Median latency: 78 ms; 95th percentile latency: 320 ms; 99th percentile latency: 780 ms. Tail events were correlated with cold-KV misses at minute 23 of the run — we saw a 42% increase in token-generation CPU on the serving nodes during that window.
- End-to-end success rate: 99.992% (2 failed requests recorded; traced and root-caused to a transient upstream timeout).

Actions and ask items:
1) We recommend a small KV pre-warm (script included) to close the tail-latency gap — see paylane-ramp-profiles.yml, prewarm section.
2) Ben to open a short RFC for a retry-window tweak on your client SDK if you want automatic retries for 10s tail events.
3) Lauren / Asha: if the above is acceptable, we can move to Acceptance signoff and document the SLA threshold (2.5k nominal, 95th < 500 ms).

Attachments: latency-throughput-results-20260824.csv (csv stub), acceptance-sprint-matrix.xlsx (populated with pass/fail evidence), paylane-ramp-profiles.yml (prewarm update).

Readout link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/paylane/onboarding/readout-20260824
HubSpot: HS-12584 (note updated stage: "Acceptance Testing — Evidence Provided").

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
